knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

## Setup

Libraries
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(tidytuesdayR)
library(janitor)
library(ggtext)
library(systemfonts)
library(showtext)
library(scales)
library(tidytext)

options(scipen = 999)

```

Fonts
```{r}
font_add_google(
  name = "Inter", 
  family = "inter"
)

font_add_google(
  name = "PT Sans Caption", 
  family = "ptsans"
)

# enable `ggplot` to use google fonts
showtext.auto()

main_font <- "inter"

```

## Data

```{r}
tuesdata <- tidytuesdayR::tt_load('2026-04-21')

financing_schemes <- tuesdata$financing_schemes
health_spending <- tuesdata$health_spending
spending_purpose <- tuesdata$spending_purpose

```


## Tidy & Explore

Health spending
```{r}
health_spending |> 
  group_by(expenditure_type) |> 
  summarise(n = n())

health_spending |> 
  filter(country_name == 'Afghanistan' & year == 2002)

health_spending |> 
  group_by(country_name) |> 
  summarise(n=n())

```

Spending purpose
```{r}
spending_purpose |> 
  arrange(desc(value))

# explore preventative vs curative 
spending_purpose |> 
  group_by(spending_purpose) |> 
  summarise(n = n())

spending_purpose |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = spending_purpose, y= value)) + 
  geom_boxplot() + 
  coord_flip()

spending_purpose |> 
  filter(iso3_code == "USA" & unit == 'constant 2023 US$') |> #USA
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = value, color = spending_purpose)) + 
  geom_line() + 
  labs(title = "USA Healthcare Spending") + 
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_number(scale = 1e-12), 
                     limits = c(0,4e12))

spending_purpose |> 
  filter(iso3_code == "CHN" & unit == 'constant 2023 US$') |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = value, color = spending_purpose)) + 
  geom_line() + 
  labs(title = "China Healthcare Spending") + 
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_number(scale = 1e-12), 
                     limits = c(0,4e12))


```

In both US and China, curative care spending between 2026 and 2022 outpaced all other healthcare spending combined. In both countries, it has risen sharply since 2016. 

## Plot

```{r}
final_plot <- 
  spending_purpose |> 
  filter(iso3_code %in% c("CHN", "USA") &  unit == 'constant 2023 US$' & year <= 2021 & year >= 2018) |> 
  mutate(spending_purpose_group = case_when(spending_purpose == "Curative care" ~ "Curative care", 
                                            spending_purpose == "Preventive care" ~ "Preventive care", 
                                            TRUE ~ "Other")) |> 
  mutate(iso3_code = case_when(iso3_code == "CHN" ~ "China", 
                             iso3_code == "USA" ~ "United States", 
                             .default = NA)) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = value, color = spending_purpose_group)) + 
  geom_line() + 
  geom_point() + 
  facet_wrap(~iso3_code, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Curative care" = "#FC8D62", "Preventive care" = "#0284C7")) + 
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_dollar(scale_cut = cut_short_scale()), 
                     limits = c(0,4e12)) + 
  scale_linewidth_manual(
    values = c(
      "Curative Care"   = 1.3,  # Thickest line for the primary hero
      "Preventive Care" = 1.1,  # Slightly thinner for the secondary hero
      "Other"           = 0.5   # Thin background lines
    )
  ) +
  labs(title = "United States Outspends China more than 5x on <span style='color:#FC8D62;'>Curative Care</span>. Preventive Care Spending Trails far Behind in Both Nations", 
       x = "Year",
       y = "Healthcare Spending") + 
  theme_classic() + 
  theme(panel.border = element_rect(color = "darkgray", fill = NA, linewidth = 1), 
        text = element_text(family = main_font),
        legend.position = "none",
        plot.title = element_markdown(face = "bold", 
                                  size = 14), 
) 

final_plot

```




## Save

```{r}
ggsave(".png", plot = final_plot, 
  width = 7,       #  inches wide
  height = 5,      # inches high
  units = "in",    # Explicitly use inches
  dpi = 150       # High resolution for print/presentation)
)

```
